topics.label: Introduction to cancer hallmarks and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture's learning objectives, the tumour progression model, and the framework of cancer hallmarks.

topics.label: Deregulated growth signaling pathways in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the deregulation of cell surface receptors and intracellular signaling cascades that drive sustained proliferative signaling.

topics.label: Block in terminal differentiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how blocks in terminal differentiation prevent cells from exiting the cell cycle across haematological and epithelial tissues.

topics.label: Evasion of apoptosis and p53 regulation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details how cancer cells evade programmed cell death through mutations in p53 and imbalance between pro- and anti-apoptotic proteins.

topics.label: Replicative immortality, senescence, and growth-control summary
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer cells overcome replicative limits via telomere maintenance and senescence bypass, concluding the discussion on growth-control hallmarks.

topics.label: Altered cellular metabolism and oncometabolites
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer cells rewire metabolic pathways toward aerobic glycolysis and produce oncometabolites that drive tumorigenesis.

topics.label: Induction of tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses how growing tumors overcome nutrient and oxygen deprivation by triggering angiogenic signaling to recruit new blood vessels.

topics.label: Mechanisms, inefficiency, and genomics of metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the multi-step process of systemic cancer dissemination, the seed and soil hypothesis, and the genomic profiling of metastatic clones.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by summarising how hallmarks co-occur across cancers and offering recommended reading.
